title: The one “I” of both natures
english: A homily by Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, on the text, “I am going to my Father; and whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son” (John 14:12–13). In the statements made about both his divinity and his humanity, he places the “I,” so that the meaning of the words is shown by their sequence, while the discernment of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said. And because he speaks in both cases as though about one person, he signifies the union of the person.
